title: Supported-section kernels on affine blowup base-change charts
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $I=(f_0,\ldots,f_r)\subseteq A$ be a finitely generated ideal, and let $x\in A$. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $Z=V(I)$, $D=V(x)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $b:S'=\operatorname{Bl}_I(S)\to S$ [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Let $f:X\to S$ be any scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Put $T=X\times_SS'$ with projections $p,q$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and let $\mathcal K,\mathcal L\subseteq p^*\mathcal F$ [def-pc-module-pullback] be the subsheaves of sections vanishing off $q^{-1}b^{-1}(Z)$ and $q^{-1}b^{-1}(Z\cup D)$, respectively. For every $a=f_i$ and affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$ with $\mathcal F|_U=\widetilde M$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], put $B=A[I/a]$ [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring], $C=C_a(A,R,I)=R\otimes_AB$ [def-nagata-strict-transform-basechange-chart-ring], and $N=M\otimes_R C\cong M\otimes_A B$. The fibre products $W=U\times_S\operatorname{Spec}B\cong\operatorname{Spec}C$ form an affine open cover of $T$. On each $W$, the pullback module is $\widetilde N$, the two closed subsets are $V(a)$ and $V(xa)$, and the two subsheaves identify, including their inclusions into $\widetilde N$, as
$$\mathcal K|_W=\widetilde{\Gamma_{(a)}(N)},\qquad \mathcal L|_W=\widetilde{\Gamma_{(xa)}(N)}.$$
Here $\Gamma_{(t)}(N)=\{n:\exists k\ge0,\ t^kn=0\}$ [def-nagata-power-torsion], with $a,x$ acting through $A\to C$. Neither $x$-torsion-freeness of $M$ nor regularity of $x$ is required.

proof.text: By [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover], the charts $\operatorname{Spec}B$ for the chosen generators cover $S\prime$. Choose affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ trivializing $\mathcal F$ as an associated module; these cover $X$ by [pqf-def-coherent]. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], their inverse images under $p$ and the blowup charts\' inverse images under $q$ are open in $T$. Their intersections are $W=U\times_S\operatorname{Spec}B$ by the fibre-product universal property. They cover $T$, since each point lies over a member of each cover. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $W=\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_A B)=\operatorname{Spec}C$, with the stated structural maps.

source.place: Tag 0804, lemma-blowing-up-affine; schemes.tex Tags 01I4/01JQ, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes/lemma-fibre-product-affines, and 01JY, lemma-base-change-immersion

proof.text: Put $H=p^*\mathcal F$. It is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] to the affine pair $W\subseteq p^{-1}U$: its natural map identifies $H(W)$ with $M\otimes_R C=N$. The counit isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] therefore identifies $H|_W$ with $\widetilde N$. The alternative module presentation is explicit: $m\otimes(r\otimes b)\mapsto rm\otimes b$ has inverse $m\otimes b\mapsto m\otimes(1\otimes b)$; balancing gives well-defined inverse maps $M\otimes_R(R\otimes_A B)\cong M\otimes_A B$.

proof.text: In the subalgebra $B=A[I/a]\subseteq A_a$ of [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring], each $f_j/a$ belongs to $B$ and $a(f_j/a)=f_j$. Thus $IB\subseteq aB$, and $a\in I$ gives the reverse inclusion. Extension to $C$ gives $IC=aC$. A prime of $C$ lies over $V(I)$ exactly when it contains every image of $I$, hence exactly when it contains $a$. Also it lies over $V(x)$ exactly when it contains $x$. Primality gives $V(a)\cup V(x)=V(xa)$. These are precisely the two closed subsets in the assertion, independently of any zero divisors in $C$.

source.place: Tag 0804, lemma-blowing-up-affine; Tag 080H, lemma-strict-transform-different-centers, affine reduction of (2)

proof.text: For $t=a$ and for $t=xa$ on $W=\operatorname{Spec}C$, the open $D(t)$ is retrocompact. Indeed on any affine open $V\subseteq W$ its intersection is the principal open of $t|_V$; [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open] identifies its topology with a spectrum, which is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact]. Restricting the definition of $\mathcal K$ or $\mathcal L$ to opens of $W$ gives exactly the supported-section subsheaf $H_t$ for $V(t)$. Apply [lem-trf-supported-sections-quasi-coherent] on $W$: $H_t$ is quasi-coherent and $H_t(W)=\{n\in N:(t)^k n=0\text{ for some }k\geq0\}$. Since $(t)^k=(t^k)$, this is precisely $\Gamma_{(t)}(N)$ as a submodule of $N$ [def-nagata-power-torsion].

source.place: Tag 07ZP, lemma-sections-supported-on-closed-subset (2)-(3); algebra.tex Tag 00E8, lemma-quasi-compact, and principal-localization spectrum identification as cited in lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open

proof.text: Apply the counit of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] to the quasi-coherent sheaves $H_t$ and $H|_W$. Its naturality identifies $H_t\hookrightarrow H|_W$ with the associated sheaf of the actual inclusion $\Gamma_{(t)}(N)\hookrightarrow N$: both maps correspond under the stated Hom bijection to that inclusion on global sections. Taking $t=a$ and $t=xa$ gives the two asserted subsheaf identifications, including their inclusions. No step required $x$ to be regular or $M$ to have zero $x$-torsion.
